A single almost-sure path continuity statement holds for the whole nonnegative time domain. The real test g is continuous, and the drift field A is jointly continuous in time and state. M is a real martingale for the stated filtration and law. For each fixed t, the displayed pathwise increment identity holds almost surely at that t.

conclusion.original: Let P be a probability law on a measurable sample space and E a compact second-countable topological space with its Borel sigma algebra. Let X be a jointly measurable process on nonnegative time with values in E and continuous paths almost surely. Let g be a continuous real test, A a jointly continuous real field on time and state, and M a real martingale for a filtration on nonnegative time under P. Suppose that for each fixed t≥0, the increment g(X_t)−g(X_0) equals the time integral of A(v,X_v) plus M_t−M_0 almost surely. At every s≥0, the expectation of g(X_t) has derivative within the nonnegative half-line equal to the expectation of A(s,X_s). Formula: \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=s,\ t\geq0}\mathbb E_P[g(X_t)]=\mathbb E_P[A(s,X_s)]
conclusion.reconstructed: Let Fexp(t)=∫_Omega g(X(max(t,0),omega)) dP(omega) for t∈R. Then HasDerivWithinAt(Fexp, ∫_Omega A(s,X(s,omega)) dP(omega), [0,infinity), s).
